description: Cache far-field multipole summaries and refresh them on predicted error events instead of every tick. This reframes tree maintenance as an event-driven problem, borrowing the sparsity mindset of event-driven molecular dynamics for a force law that is otherwise continuously evaluated.
mathematical_formalization: Schedule refresh tau_c = min{t : ||M_c(t) - M_c(t_last)|| > delta_M or topology(c) changes}; use a_i(t) = a_near(t) + a_far(M(t_last)) until t >= tau_c
analogical_connections: Dirty-rectangle rendering refreshes only changed screen regions; here only stale force summaries are recomputed.
Event-driven hard-sphere molecular dynamics becomes event-driven multipole refresh.
An incremental build system mirrors selective invalidation of distant gravity caches.
implementation_hypothesis: Store center-of-mass and multipole summaries with velocity bounds per node; predict when each summary exits its error budget; push refresh events into a priority queue; rebuild globally only when invalidations become too dense.
experiment_seed: Use a quasi-stable solar-system scene and a chaotic scattering scene; measure tree-refresh count, wall-clock time, and trajectory error versus rebuilding every frame.

closest_prior_art.title: Application of event-driven molecular dynamics approach to rarefied gas dynamics problems
Cold atom-ion systems in radio-frequency multipole traps: Event-driven molecular dynamics and stochastic simulations
A hierarchical O(N log N) force-calculation algorithm

novelty_claim: The novelty is not event-driven pairwise gravity, but event-driven maintenance of approximate distant structure, which matches the update patterns of interactive scenes.
differentiation: Event-driven molecular dynamics papers schedule actual collisions or interaction events. This concept schedules when a cached approximation becomes too stale, so it changes the bookkeeping layer rather than the physical force law itself.
